function: Predictive beamforming: directly predicts the RSMA precoder and common-rate allocation from historical CSI for a LEO satellite downlink, maximizing weighted ergodic sum rate. p. 1, p. 5
system: Single LEO satellite with Nt=4 antennas serving K=4 single-antenna terminals, 1-layer RSMA, FDD, Ka-band 28 GHz, 500 MHz, 550 km altitude; no RIS. p. 3, p. 5, p. 9
method: TranCN: Transformer plus CNN fusion, trained end to end with Adam on negative weighted sum rate as loss (unsupervised, no labels), in-orbit training. p. 6-9
data_channel: Own simulator: Shadowed-Rician fading with free-space loss, time-correlated CSI, 28 GHz LEO at 550 km; generated samples split 70% training, 30% test. p. 4, p. 9
test_conditions: 70/30 split of the same simulated dataset; sweeps over SNR, number of UTs, antennas and history length, with no stated reuse of a trained model. p. 9-11
baselines: Non-learned: SCA precoder design under outdated CSIT. Learned: MLP, CNN, RNN, LSTM, GRU and Transformer adapted to the same task. p. 9-10
metrics: Weighted ergodic sum rate versus SNR, number of UTs, antennas and history length; CPU time for precoder design; training loss convergence. p. 10-12
complexity: Big-O order of Transformer and CNN modules versus SCA interior-point O((KNtY)^3.5 log(1/eps)); measured CPU time in milliseconds versus minutes for SCA. p. 9, p. 11
openness: none; samples come from the authors' own simulator (p. 9) and no link to code or data appears in the paper.
q1_support: p. 9: "historical CSI samples are generated based on the channel model delineated in Section II". Section II (p. 4) defines a custom Shadowed-Rician model with free-space loss and time-correlated updates, Table II lists 28 GHz and 550 km; no 3GPP TR 38.811, ray-traced or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "the entire dataset is partitioned into training and testing sets at a ratio of 70% to 30%" (held-out part of the same data). Figs. 4-7 sweep SNR, UTs, antennas and history length, but the input size 2KNt (p. 7) ties a model to one K and Nt, and the paper never says a trained model is reused in a new setting.
q3_support: p. 9: "we establish a robust benchmark by integrating SCA, as detailed in [46], for precoder design under outdated CSIT"; p. 10: "(1) MLP, (2) CNN, (3) Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), (4) LSTM, (5) GRU, and (6) Transformer". All are compared with TranCN on WESR in Figs. 4-7.
q4_support: p. 9: "represents the total computational complexity" (Big-O of the Transformer and CNN modules, against SCA); p. 11: "the average Central Processing Unit (CPU) time consumed for precoder design" (measured, milliseconds versus minutes).
q5_support: p. 9: "historical CSI samples are generated based on the channel model delineated in Section II". The data come from the authors' own simulator; no code or data link, DOI or availability statement appears in the text or the references.
notes: Checked: p. 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TWC.2024.3486673. Area 6 rather than 3: the learned precoder prediction serves a LEO satellite downlink, and NTN is the more specific area. q2 judged 0 because the sweeps over UTs and antennas change the input size of the model and the paper does not say a trained model is tested in an unseen configuration; reviewer to confirm. Table II was read from the page image (p. 9).
